What Kind of Cost It Removes

Every row in the right column is behaviour this extension already ships, not a roadmap promise

Two ways to do the same thing — before installing on the left, after on the right
Scenario Without it With it
Accounts across environments Four accounts for dev / test / staging / prod of the same system sit side by side and overwrite each other during autofill — filling the wrong environment happens all the time. Matching defaults to the exact hostname, so the four environments never cross over; when one account really does serve them all, widen the tier by one.
Two-step verification The password is in the manager and the code is on your phone: mid-login you switch apps, hunt for the entry and copy six digits — and if the code expires, start over. The TOTP secret lives in the same entry as the password. On the code page the live-code pill anchors automatically — click Fill and the second step is done.
Pages that refuse to fill Self-built login pages, legacy systems, inputs inside a Shadow DOM — the browser cannot recognise them, so you type everything by hand. Point the account / password fields at your own CSS selectors for that domain, reaching into Shadow DOM; export the rules as JSON and hand them to teammates.
Where the passwords live Cloud storage means accepting "the server may be breached" as a premise, plus a subscription for multi-device sync. Five sensitive fields are encrypted individually with AES-256-GCM and written only to local chrome.storage.local — no cloud, no account, no subscription.
Moving in Migrating out of another password manager means retyping everything by hand, or giving up on the export format. Export formats from Chrome / LastPass / Bitwarden / 1Password are detected automatically, as CSV or JSON, in about 30 seconds.
Which passwords to change Reused, too weak, long since leaked — you never know unless you check each one, and by the time something breaks it is too late. One click gives a 0-100 offline score, weighted across reuse / weak / commonly leaked / long-unupdated — every calculation stays on your machine.

Core Features

From encrypted storage to smart filling, from 2FA to health checks — the full lifecycle of your credentials in one place

Local Encryption — Passwords Never Leave the Browser

The master password derives a 256-bit key via PBKDF2 (600,000 iterations); username, password, URL, remark and TOTP are each stored as ciphertext. Locking and session expiry destroy only the session key material — the vault is already ciphertext at rest, and no password content is ever uploaded. Every master password field also warns live when Caps Lock is on, so a case typo never looks like a wrong password.

PBKDF2 · 600K iterations AES-256-GCM No password uploads Idle / restart auto-lock

Four Ways to Fill — One Click

Pick your style: the in-field inline mini panel (default), the side panel, the right-click menu, or the quick-fill shortcut. Quadruple fill strategies work on React / Vue and classic pages alike; exact domain matching separates test environments, the side panel toggles between this-site and all-entry search, and auto-login after filling is optional.

Side panel Ctrl+Shift+L Inline panel Ctrl+Shift+K Quick fill Ctrl+Shift+F Right-click fill Auto login trigger Password visibility toggle One-click share card

Smart Login Form Detection

Automatically detects username, password, phone, and verification-code fields (including cross-iframe), and can auto-check options like "Remember me" and "Agree to terms".

TOTP Two-Factor Codes

Add a secret by scanning an on-page QR code or uploading an image; codes are generated locally (RFC 6238, zero network) with live codes and countdowns in the list, side panel and inline panel, plus one-click fill / copy — split two-step logins auto-hand off a live-code capsule on the code page.

283 914

Security Health Dashboard

One click yields a 0–100 score from four weighted dimensions: reuse (35), weak (25), commonly leaked (20, offline dictionary) and stale (20); missing 2FA is flagged but unscored — with expiry reminders, all computed locally.

82

Auto-Save Login Credentials

Chrome-style credential capture with a confirmation prompt on login; edit tag and remark in the prompt; allowlist/blocklist matching, fingerprint-based dedup, and one-click "Never for this site"; weak and reused passwords are flagged inline in the prompt (a heads-up only — saving is never blocked).

Import, Export & Encrypted Backup

CSV / JSON formats with auto-detection of Chrome, LastPass, Bitwarden, and 1Password exports; encrypted .aph backup export/import, plus email backup with scheduled reminders.

Tags, Favorites & Smart Search

Multi-select tags with stable colors, tag filtering, pinned favorites (configurable limit + LRU eviction), multi-field smart search (pinyin / initials + match highlighting) and sorting, one-click dedup, and batch delete / tag editing / export of selected entries — plus a read-only "View details" drawer for the full remark and password history, no edit mode needed. Long lists stay organized.

Dual-Mode Password Generator

Random passwords (length, character sets, ambiguous-character exclusion) and passphrases (a bundled 3,080-word list) — cryptographically secure via Web Crypto, with a live strength bar.

Trash & Password History

Deleted entries stay in the trash for 30 days and can be restored anytime (newest deletion first, with keyword search); password history is configurable (enable/disable, 1–10 encrypted snapshots per entry, default 3) for one-click rollback; changing the master password re-keys atomically without data loss.

Themes & Bilingual UI

6 color themes and instant Chinese/English switching; entries show site favicons (read from the browser's local cache, zero network) for faster recognition in long lists.

Identity Vault

A standalone locker for personal details — name, ID number, phone, email, address, bank card (number / issuing bank / holder / expiry / CVV) and custom fields — encrypted as one AES-256-GCM blob with secret fields masked by default and a master-password re-check to open. Copy a single field or the whole card in one click (the clipboard auto-clears on a timer), batch-show / hide secrets and collapse or expand all cards, search with pinyin matching and a match count, export a checked subset, get an on-save possible-duplicate reminder, and see the 30-record cap. Encrypted .aphid backup export/import, plus an optional plaintext .json export / re-import gated by a master-password re-check and a risk confirmation; it is not covered by automatic backups, so export an encrypted backup regularly.

Site Rules Fallback

Login fields hidden inside custom components? Under "Site rules" on the manager page, pin the CSS selectors for that domain's username and password inputs (the rule domain must equal the login page domain exactly). Every rule carries a "Shadow DOM penetration" switch, on by default, that reaches open shadow roots only. Rules export as plain-text JSON (domains and selectors, never credentials) and merge-import by domain, so a team can share one working set instead of configuring browser by browser.

Three Cross-Subdomain Tiers

By default only entries on the exact host are shown. "Exact + wildcard entries" makes an account saved as *.qq.com appear on any subdomain of that site; "Same main domain" adds a fallback — when the current host has no account of its own, entries from the apex domain and sibling subdomains are offered, badged "cross-subdomain". Widening changes only which entries are offered and fillable; the auto-save duplicate rule is deliberately tier-independent.

How it works

The four steps one fill takes on your own machine, from opening a login page to saving a new credential

1

Read the login page

The content script works out which fields are username, password and one-time code. Scanning is throttled and batched, and never rewrites the host page’s styles or scripts.

2

Pick candidates by domain

Three cross-subdomain tiers decide which accounts appear in the side panel and the inline dropdown. Exact host match is the default, so dev / test / staging / prod entries never mix.

3

Decrypt locally

The master password derives a key through PBKDF2. Opening a list decrypts the vault once, and the plaintext lives only in the extension’s own context — the disk keeps ciphertext. Key material and decrypted snapshots are destroyed on lock or expiry.

4

Fill, then sign in

Fields are written one by one, consent and “remember me” boxes get ticked, and the sign-in button can be clicked for you if you switch that on. A credential seen for the first time always asks before it is saved.

Get Started in Four Steps

No sign-up, no login — download and go

01

Install the Extension

Install with one click from the Chrome Web Store (recommended — auto-updates). If you can't access Google, download the zip from GitHub Releases and install manually. After installation the key icon appears in the toolbar.

02

Set a Master Password

On first use, set a master password of at least 8 characters with letters, numbers, and special characters — your only key.

03

Add or Import Passwords

Add accounts manually, or bulk import via the CSV template or a JSON file; tags keep everything organized.

04

Enjoy Auto-Fill

Open a login page and click the key icon inside the login field (inline fill, the default) — or fill via the side panel or the quick-fill shortcut (Ctrl+Shift+F).

Updating: simply overwrite the files in the original installation directory with the files from the new zip. Never load the extension from a different directory — Chrome would treat it as a fresh install and your existing password data would become inaccessible.

💡 How to find the current installation directory: open chrome://extensions/, find this extension's card, click "Details", and look for "Source: /path/to/your/directory" near the bottom — that path is the installation directory to overwrite when updating.

Developers: several environments in parallel Keep the default tier and the accounts on fat.example.com and uat.example.com stay strictly apart. "Cross-subdomain matching" in the password manager header
QA: one account shared across subdomains Widen one tier to "exact match + wildcard entries" and decide entry by entry which URLs are written as *.qq.com. Same place; all three tiers switch anytime

Moving in from another manager CSV and JSON imports, with Chrome / LastPass / Bitwarden / 1Password export formats detected automatically. "Import data" on the manager page
A new machine or a reinstalled OS Export an .aph encrypted backup and carry it along; on import it decrypts to a preview before you confirm. "Data management" on the manager page

Checking regularly which passwords to change A one-click 0-100 offline audit that lists what to fix across four weighted dimensions, all computed locally. "Security audit" on the manager page

Installation and Requirements

One click in the store, or load the unpacked folder offline — both paths use exactly the same data format

Runtime

A recent desktop Google Chrome / Edge (Manifest V3). Installing from Chrome Web Store is recommended, since updates arrive automatically; when Google is unreachable, download the zip from GitHub Releases and load it manually.

The repo also ships pnpm build:firefox (an MV2 build), but releases and verification target Chrome. As with any extension, chrome:// pages, Web Store pages and other extensions' pages cannot be injected.

Chrome Web Store Download zip

Loading offline (four steps)

  • Download the latest zip from Releases and unpack it into a folder you will keep.
  • Open chrome://extensions/ and turn on Developer mode in the top-right corner.
  • Click "Load unpacked extension" and pick the folder from the previous step.
  • When updating, overwrite the same folder — a different path makes Chrome treat it as a brand-new install (see the update note under the four-step guide above).

Build environment

Node.js ^20.19.0 || >=22.12.0 (the floor comes from Vite; CI pins Node 22) and pnpm 10 (see packageManager). The stack is WXT + Vue 3 + TypeScript + Element Plus + Vite, with Element Plus imported per component to keep the bundle small, and matching plus crypto logic covered by Vitest.

pnpm dev         # dev server
pnpm build       # production build
pnpm test:run    # unit tests
pnpm typecheck   # tsc --noEmit
pnpm lint        # ESLint
pnpm lint:style  # Stylelint

Privacy & permissions

“Password data stays on this machine” has to be checkable, not just claimed. These are the four reasons it holds.

  • Each of the five sensitive fields is encrypted on its own before it reaches chrome.storage.local. Locking and session expiry only destroy key material and decrypted snapshots — the vault is never re-encrypted wholesale.
  • The only outbound request is an anonymous version check every 6 hours that reads nothing but a published version number. Accounts, passwords and one-time codes never travel on that channel.
  • Neither cookies nor history are requested. The content script works on login forms only, and the UI it injects is sealed inside a closed Shadow DOM that neither reads nor writes page variables.
  • Everything leaves with you: CSV / JSON exports and .aph encrypted backups stay in your hands, so a new machine needs your own backup file rather than a sync service.
<all_urls> Detect login forms and offer autofill on any website (host permission, scoped as described above)
activeTab Detect login forms and perform auto-fill on the current tab
clipboardRead Read clipboard to verify content has not been replaced before auto-clearing
webNavigation Monitor page navigation events to optimize form detection timing

Cross-origin Proxy
